question.text: If enthalpy of atomization for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is <math><mi mathvariant="normal">x </mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and bond enthalpy for <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is <math><mi mathvariant="normal">y </mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, the relation between them

solution.text:
∆Hatomisation=∆HVap+Bond Energy
Hence x>y

Enthalpy of atomization is enthalpy change involved when one mole of gaseous atom is formed from a substance in an elemental state (Elemental state of Bromine is Br2(l)).

While, bond energy is energy required to break one mole of bonds in gaseous state to form separated atoms.
